name: Crystal Pepsi
tierWhy: PepsiCo withdrew the original clear cola in 1994, but it has put the Crystal Pepsi name back on bottles in limited runs: a 2015 sweepstakes, retail releases in 2016 and 2017, and a 2022 contest.[^19][^25][^30][^32][^34]

dates.text: was announced as a clear cola going into test markets in Providence, Dallas and Colorado
got a rival when Coca-Cola unveiled Tab Clear at the Hayden Planetarium in New York
opened its national advertising during Super Bowl XXVII
returned to US store shelves for a limited run, 22 years after it was withdrawn

title: Crystal Pepsi (1992–1994): post-mortem · Spectre Brands
description: A clear cola, a Super Bowl launch and a rival that says it was built to fail, traced from PepsiCo’s annual reports and the press of 1992–1994 to the nostalgia re-releases.

card.blurb: Pepsi took the color out of cola, put about $40 million of advertising behind it and projected $1 billion in sales. Within a year the product was being reworked. The name now comes back for a few weeks at a time.

stat.label: estimated launch advertising, for a drink reworked within a year

hero.dates: Test-marketed from April 1992. National in December 1992. Reformulated and renamed in 1994.
hero.standfirst: The slogan was “You’ve never seen a taste like this.” A year later, most people had stopped looking.
hero.deck: Crystal Pepsi was a caffeine-free cola with no caramel coloring, launched nationally with an estimated $40 million of advertising and a Super Bowl spot. Pepsi projected more than 2% of a $47 billion market. By PepsiCo’s own account the brand helped one quarter, softened, and was sent back to be “refined.”
hero.artCaption: Original illustration of a clear cola bottle. Not an official asset and not the trademarked label.

findings.title: The test markets worked.
findings.text: A grocery clerk in Rhode Island said it was “blowing off the shelves” in May 1992, while one chain sold two-liter bottles for 39 cents with coupons against a usual $1.49.[^6]

findings.title: Pepsi promised a third cola category.
findings.text: It projected more than 2% of the market in the first national year, about $1 billion at retail, on an estimated $40 million of advertising.[^8]

findings.title: The boost lasted one quarter.
findings.text: PepsiCo told shareholders the Crystal Pepsi products “particularly aided first quarter results, but did not significantly impact full year profits.”[^2]

findings.title: It was not Pepsi without the color.
findings.text: Pepsi said so at launch. Its creator later said: “It would have been nice if I’d made sure the product tasted good.”[^5][^20]

findings.title: The name outlived the drink.
findings.text: PepsiCo brought it back in 2015, 2016, 2017 and 2022, each time as a limited release sold on nostalgia.[^25][^30][^32][^34]
